root: ^On the unfortunate occasion that a person is in a traumatic situation, especially one as pertaining to a crime, accident, mishap, mistreatment, etc. it is often useful to record a testimonial.
^Given what happened, we'd like to request a statement from you.

^To be blunt, I'd like to know what on earth could have happened that night. None of the story makes sense, so many details that just don't add up, so many people who just don't recall things I can't believe anyone would miss.

^I'm going to require that you take a Witness Competency Exam. I'm sorry that it's come to this, but my only possible explaination at this point is that some of the eyewitnesses must have hit their heads the day of the incident, have a strange case of collective narcolepsy, or perhaps they've contracted some crazy disease that's melted the part of their brain that's in touch with reality. Whatever it is, I need to know if I can trust what you say.
^Check the box below to confirm that you understand.

g-0: ^Question 1: Do you agree with the following statement: "No person is perfect. Therefore, I am not perfect. Therefore, I understand that as a witness, there are times I can be wrong about things. Therefore, if my lawyer were to offer clarification about something I believe I saw, no matter how sure I am that I saw what I believe I saw, I understand that my Lawyer is probably right since this is his job after all and I will correct my testimony to reflect my Lawyer's better judgement."

s: ^I disagree with the statement because I believe I am perfect.
^I disagree with the statement because I think I know better than a lawyer, despite not getting the degree, knowing the law, or doing this whole thing for a living.

g-1: ^Question 2: Do you believe in justice? Do you believe that every criminal deserves a sentence, even if that criminal is a grandmother, a toddler, or a nun?

s: ^I believe some people are beyond the law.

g-2: ^Question 3: Are you familiar with the following words?
^Algebra, Pacific, Havana, Muscle, Icebox, Bacteria, Lipid, Cumulonimbus, Heron, Fire

s: ^I've looked up the word "Uneducated" and it describes me.

g-3: ^Question 4: Do you have a history of associating with unsavory groups that would lead your testimony to face scrutiny among a reasonable jury? Examples include the following: Communists, Nudists, Protestants, Utopians, Environmentalists

s: ^I associate with one or more of those groups.
^I have a history but I can demonstrate reformation.
^I can set aside my Protestantism for the puproses of justice.

g-4: ^Question 5: Do you agree to refrain from communicating with other witnesses?

b: ^Oh my, it appears that the two of you answered every single answer the same. I'll have to keep my records straight. How strange.

arthurbegin: ^It's a strangely chilly morning on a shipping dock on the coast. I'm with a small crowd of wealthy travelers, awaiting the moment the crew is ready to leave. No one is really suprised about the delays, expeditions tend to be like that, but the predictable nature of it doesn't make anyone happy about it.
^I look around for something to do.
watch: ^The time is 10:48 AM. Just 2 minutes since the last time I checked. That is 2 hours and 48 minutes since we were originally told we would leave, and 22 minutes since the last estimated time to leave.
staff: ^I search around for someone who could be part of the staff. There's no one to be seen. They've likely retreated to the boat to avoid angry customers trying to figure out what's going on.
timeout1: ^I'm paralyzed by indecision. I need to get it together, but these long waits always bother me. I close my eyes and take a deep breath as I try to compose myself.
next1: ^And so I look around for something important to do. Until I'm suddenly interrupted. I feel a man tap my shoulder. A heavy tap. It's a very big hand.
^"Pardon me, have you seen my wife?" He asks me. He's the only one I've met with an accent, which is especially strange for a boat that's leaving from the mexican coast.

c-2: ^"Can you tell me about her features? Skin tone, hieght, eye or hair color?" I ask him.

nameoutfit: ^"Don't know, haven't met her." He tells me, laughing as he does. He's got a few friends around him, laughing along. "But i've seen her on the boat. I reckon we'll be married by the first day and divorced by the time we get back to shore!"
^He smells like he's been drinking quite a bit. I suspect the man might believe we're already at sea.
description: ^"Slow down friend, you sound like policia! The girl is still alive. And if I'm lucky, the girl will meet me soon and we will fall in love, and be happily married, honeymooned, and divorced in no time." He laughs and punches me, in a friendly way. A drunkard friendly way. It stings. A few people who seem to be his friends laugh along with him.
^He's right, I do sound like policia. I need to keep a better profile.
timeout2: ^I struggle to talk for a moment. No words come to mind. "I haven't met you, or your wife," I tell him.

^He smiles. "I haven't met her either. But I plan on honeymooning after we meet and get married tonight. if you slow down on the drinking, you could see the wedding yourself tonight!" His friends gathered around him are laughing with him.
^I haven't been drinking. I'm just struggling to speak today. He, on the other hand, sounds like he's been really going for it.
elizabeth: ^The man points. "Oh, there she is now! up there."
^A woman sits on the top of the bridge to the boat. "Attention everyone!" She says.

b: ^"There's been a weather delay! Expect another 30 minutes before the boat can set out."
^The crowd groans. There's yelling and cursing. The man beside me is the loudest to yell. "There's not a cloud in the sky!" he says.
^"There's been a delay for maintenance! Expect another 30 minutes before the boat can set out."
^The crowd groans. There's yelling and cursing. The man beside me is the loudest to yell. "I should start swimming! I'd probably reach Havana before the boat does."
^"There's been a delay! A mess in the Kitchen."
^The man besides me shouts back. "A mess? What kind of mess?"
^She seems flustered. "We had some food spoil. It's quite bad, it will be about 30 minutes to clean and get ready to leave."
^"30 minutes!?" another person says. "Good heavens, put me in the kitchen and I'll clean it in 5!"
^She shakes her head. "No, I apologize sir, we have professionals handling it now. Please stand by and we'll head out soon!"

cleanerintro: ^I've been aboard the Heron a few hours now. I've found my room, toured the deck, and at the moment I'm brandishing a cowboy hat near the stern. I was told the signal would be obvious, and yet here I stand, avoiding sun exposure as best I can, but I'm not noticing anyone.

^I was supposed to meet my contact when the boat set sail. As I look back the shore is completely gone. The contact is obviously delayed. I'm starting to wonder if they've found trouble or if they need help.
^A young boy shows up. He's looking me directly in the eyes. He can't be much older than 17 years old.
^"Arthur Whitlock! I'm so glad that you're here." He says.
cleanerlate: ^"Oh, yeah, I'm sorry about that. I got stuck on the job. More cleaning than what I thought. Sometimes that happens. And setoff is always busy." The boy scratches at his neck.
^"I'm James." the boy says. He sticks his hand out for a handshake.
cleanername: ^"Oh," he asks. His eyes get wide. "I'm sorry, Arthur. What should I call you instead?"
^"William" I say. It seems like a good name for a wealthy person on a luxury cruise.
^." He smiles and nods. "You can call me James. Oh, do I need a codename too?"
^"Right! I already work on the boat, so everyone knows me anyways. That's a good call."
cleanertimeout: ^"Uhh." I say. He's not exactly the contact I was expecting.
^"You're Arthur Whitlock, right?" He asks me.
^I try to get my act together.
^"Yes, I am. Sorry. just was having some issues there. Apologies."
^"No worries, Arthur. I'm just glad that you're here." He tells me. "You can call me James."
cleanerbriefing: ^"So," I ask him, "Are you going to bring me to the person who hired me?"
^James smiles. "You're looking at him." He's pointing at himself. He's very proud of himself.

s: ^"You need to tell me what's happening. Now."

cleanerafford: ^"Well," he says slowly, "I will admit I don't have all of the money, and I apologize for that, and honestly I don't even have half the money, but I thought there was real danger and I needed the best. and well... say you don't want to do it. Are you just gonna swim back?"
^I look back at the water. I am not going to swim back.
^"That's a very strange way to treat someone that you'd like to get free labor from." I shake my head.
cleanerhappening: ^He takes off the had and starts fanning his face with it.
cleanertimeout2: ^I say nothing. I'm just not feeling right.
^It's fine. I think. It's just the seasickness getting to me.
^He's noticed. "These ships can be challenging to get used to. Are you sick? It's best to let it out if it starts to happen."
^I'm doing my best not to throw up. "I'm fine, just... tell me about the case."
cleanerbriefing2: ^"The case." He scratches his ear with his shoulder. "Actually, I don't really have that much to go off. I was working with a person here. His name was Trout."
^"Trout?" I ask. It's an odd name.

^"Yeah, it's a funny story. He's one of the cleaners, the guy only had one arm. Well, one day he was mopping the deck on his first day. Well, wet floor, choppy waters that day, he's kinda by the edge, somehow and someway he goes overboard. And when we go over to take a look, we watch the guy start to swim. And he can't do it, you know, with the one arm and all. You should have seen it, it was impossible not to laugh. He looked like a fish out of water, when he was in the water. So we called him Trout." The boy is smiling ear to ear.
^The boy shakes his head. "Haven't seen him since the other night." It's hard to imagine why, he seems to have great professional partners.

s: ^"Tell me about the last time you saw him."
^"You don't seem to concerned about this."

lasttimeseen: ^"We were returning to shore to get ready for this expedition here. All enjoying our time together when Trout gets a letter. Handed to him by the ship's Navigator. I think his name is Charlie? Well, Trout gets this letter that says 'If you do it again, you're dead'. And that's it."
^"Did you ask Charlie the Navigator about it?" I ask.

^"Well, obviously, and when we did he just said that he was handed the letter in Havana. And if you really think about it, if it was a death threat from him, he would probably want to keep that fairly secret, right?"
^I nod. "That would make most sense to me."
cleanerconcern: ^"Oh, it's fairly normal for him to disappear. We don't know how he does it. But he's made a lot of enemies on the ship, and he knows how to disappear when he needs to."
^I raise an eyebrow. "Enemies? That he needs to disappear from?"

^"Oh yeah, he's got enemies. The guy always has a break up like every month. Always super messy. He's gotten caught stealing from guests, he's always getting on everyone's nerves. And I know you're gonna say 'Oh, that sounds like something you should lead with.' Well, Trout just has this way of getting out of it everytime. But I wonder what the consequences are when it catches up to him?" the boy looks up.
^I get a bit closer. "What do you think?"
^"He got handed a letter a few nights ago. Telling him 'If you do it again, you're dead.' What do you think?"
cleanertimeout3: ^"Hmm." I say. I'm having a hard time paying attention.
^"What's going on with you?" The boy asks me.
^"I think I'm just hungry for Trout."
^He shakes his head. "Maybe this was a mistake. Well, Trout got a letter saying his life was in danger. That someone was upset with him and they wanted to kill him.
^I stave off my hunger as best I can. I didn't eat enough and it's bothering me.
cleanerbriefing3: ^I clear my throat. "I think it's time we find Trout."
^The boy nods his head in agreement. "There's a party tonight, a setoff party. You should be able to meet members of the crew there. I'll see you there,
arthurparty: ^I enter the party in the ballroom of the Heron. It's not enormous, but it is quite impressive for a room on a boat, I must admit. A band plays in the corner, somehow adjusted to the way the boat is rocking over the water this evening.

^The kid wasn't able to come with, apparently no cleaners were allowed in attendance. He seemed disappointed about it, but I have to admit I wasn't entirely heartbroken about the idea of time without him. So I alone try to decide who might know something about Trout.
^I begin wandering around the party, trying to portray the same confidence and cheeriness the other passengers were showing.
^And then I saw a familiar face.
^A large man talking to a young lady at the party. She seems incredibly uncomfortable.

^"You'll have to attend one of the bullfights sometime. You've never seen extravagence until you've seen how the city gets. You seem like a girl who respects the finer things." He's got his hands on her shoulders, and she's looking anywhere but his smiling face.
^I feel it's time to do something.

c-2: ^I decide to observe, I shouldn't make any brash decisions.

appanic1: ^My mind goes blank, but I need to do something. Anything to help her escape. I do the only thing that comes to mind.
^Everyone turns. The band stops a moment. And the man is so shocked, seeing me scream and looking directly at him, he drops the girl.

^The whole room is completely silent. The man grumbles something under his breath and turns to me. His smile is gone. "Are you insane? Why do you scream sir, I am trying to enjoy my evening. Do you need something?"
^The girl looks at me, somewhat shocked.
apnone1: ^She looks tired. She's not squirming, and she's not talking. She's definitely not all there.
apleave1: ^She attempts to walk away, but he grabs her arm stopping her in place.
apsmile1: ^She makes a face. For a moment I have a hard time telling exactly what she's doing, but after a brief pause I realize she's trying to give a smile. There's no way it's a real smile, but she's trying.
aproute2: ^"What's the matter?" The man asks. "Are you ready to leave? If the party is too loud, we can go elsewhere. My room has the finest view of the whole boat."

^The man turns. "Ah, you made it! It is good to see you, I'd like you to meet Elizabeth."
^I smile and nod at her. "Now, I apologize for listening in on your conversation, but I believe you just said that you are a bullfighter, is that correct?"
^"Oh, yes." he says. "A very famous one at that. I take it you are a fan?"

^I reel a little bit. "Oh, that is not to say that I don't enjoy it. But at the end of the day, yes, I suppose it is a sport. But sports aren't exclusively kids games. In the United States of America we consider boxing a sport. A fight between men."
^He seems a bit confused. "I don't fight men, I fight bulls."
^I nod. "True. And after watching men fight bulls, I no longer claim to be a fan of boxing."
^He smiles when he hears this. Briefly.
abftcurious: ^I shrug. "I can't claim to be the biggest fan, but I've always been a little curious."
^He looks at me like I'm an alien. "You are just 'curious'? You watch men risk death to fight monstrous bulls, and you simply find yourself 'curious'?"
^I'm getting a bit nervous. "Well, I've never actually seen a fight-"
^He interrupts me. "A fan of bullfighting who's never watched a bullfight! You, sir, are a liar. You tried to deceive me, to get on my good side."
^I'm sweating now. "You misunderstand, sir, I do not wish to upset you. I wish to learn more about the fighter."
abftnointerest: ^I look away from him. "Bullfighting never seemed all that interesting to me."
^"Oh, really." He says. "So then why bother me while about it while I'm trying to enjoy my night?"
^I don't answer him. He turns to me, and I begin to realize just how much bigger he is than me.

abftalktwo: ^I try to think of what next to ask the bullfighter.

^Ask about the greatest bull he's ever fought
^Ask him what he's doing aboard the Heron

^"So, does being a famous bullfighter turn you to a creep by default, or is that something you developed on your own?"

^I see a little vein emerge on his forehead. "Bullfighting is not a decision that you make lightly one day. A person is born a bullfighter. They make every moment about training, every day about getting sharper, about living to satiate a crowd."

abftgreatest: ^"Tell me about the greatest bull you've ever fought."

^He nods. "You know the way to a bullfighter's heart. Let me tell you, the least bull I fought was the size of 6 grown men, and stood a full head and shoulders above my height. When it charged at me, I felt the ground shake, the skies split, when it passed me it felt like I was in the midst of a swirling hurricane. The bull's horns were strong enough to split stone..."
^The man talks excitedly. I look to Elizabeth as he continues.
abftwhy: ^I think aloud. "Why are you, a great bullfighter, aboard the Heron? Why are you not bullfighting now?"

^He glances around, then responds quietly. I get the impression he's trying to keep his response secret from the other guests, but he's talking loud enough that I would be suprised if anyone didn't hear.

^"Actually, sir, what's very strange is that I was given an invitation. Someone saying that they loved what I did, loved watching my last fight, and they wanted to give me a trip aboard a fancy boat. I never caught who they were, but they seemed eager to meet me. So now sir, I have to ask you. Was it you?"
^He gives me a look. I think he really thinks it was me. I decide its best to not to lie.
^I don't know whether to apologize or not.

elizabethbegin: ^It's a silent ship kitchen. I stand shoulder to shoulder with the captain - my father - who stands shoulder to shoulder with our navigator, and we're looking at a dead body in the freezer. The body sits in a box, head turned like it's watching the wall.
^There's a fork sticking out of it's shoulder. One of the nice forks, but none of us is willing to dislodge and recover it. I'm trying to look for the words to say.
^We need to call off the expedition.

c-0: ^ "We need to call off the expedition," I say.
c-1: ^ "How could this have happened?" I ask.

calloff: ^"No." My father says. "We've got a killer aboard, and from this point on, we need to think like a game of cat and mouse. Anything we think the killer might want us to do, we don't. And vice versa." He's stern, he's got a certain look in his eyes.
^"You believe that a killer did all this to convince us not to leave?" I ask him.
^The Navigator nods. "Yes. I can think of no other reason. We need to set sail immediately. Stick to open areas. Stay together."
^My father turns to me. He sees I'm not convinced. But he is. I know that there will be no changing his mind.
^"I need you to go talk to the passengers. give them some excuse. Anything. We need about 15 more minutes. Just enough time to clean up the body. Keep this secret from everyone." He tells me.
^"Don't you think the passengers could help us?" I ask.
^"Oh, Elizabeth. The passengers are immediately going to suspect us. So don't tell anyone. Understood?"

^No. I don't understand. But I nod nonetheless and start heading back to the dock. What excuse can I possibly give to push the expedition back? My father said 15 minutes, but I I figure it realistically should be double that.

^"You were the only one in the kitchen over the last day, ever since the new year's party, and we didn't notice anything then. Surely you must have seen something!" I'm begging him to remember something.
